learnings.claim: YouTube native title and thumbnail A/B test is not a Shorts experiment; Shorts packaging iteration must not be labeled as that product.
learnings.decision: Use sequential owned-channel metrics for Shorts experiments and reserve native A/B conclusions for eligible long-form only.
fallback_history: If native A/B eligibility is unclear, do not transfer the result to Shorts.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next Shorts analytics read use engaged views, retention, and AVD or APV rather than a native A/B result.
learnings.title: Native YouTube A/B tests do not cover Shorts

learnings.claim: The YouTube Reporting API recommends advancing the createdAfter cursor only after reports have been successfully processed; a cursor advanced past a failed or unprocessed report can exclude it from later incremental listings, including backfilled reports.
learnings.decision: REPORT_CREATED_AFTER_ACK_GATE: Keep createdAfter unchanged until all selected reports in the paginated batch have been downloaded, validated, and durably imported (or explicitly deduplicated). On a partial failure, retain the prior checkpoint and replay idempotently by report ID. For reports with the same job and period, retain the newest createTime as the backfill replacement; never sum old and new versions. Advance only after durable success/read-back, and record the checkpoint with the processed report IDs. Do not infer actual channel ingestion without authorized API evidence.
failure_history: Earlier attempt to stage this learning was blocked; no production ingestion or checkpoint read-back is verified.
fallback_history: Keep the previous createdAfter checkpoint and replay pending reports by ID after transient ingestion failures; if Reporting API access is unavailable, keep channel completeness unknown.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next authorized Reporting API ingestion test, simulate an older report failing after a newer report succeeds, then confirm no cursor advancement, successful replay, report-ID dedup, backfill replacement and durable read-back.
learnings.title: Reporting API createdAfter checkpoint must follow successful processing

learnings.claim: ChatGPT proposed process gate HO-06_GUMROAD_DRAFT_FIRST on 2026-10-10 (branch chatgpt/domain-promotions-20261010). It is a review/verification procedure, not verified research; no field, metric or claim in it has been checked against the cited source yet.
learnings.decision: HO-06_GUMROAD_DRAFT_FIRST: Draft original Turkish food-science digital product (Mutfağın Hammaddeleri sample/checklist); verify rights, payout eligibility, fees, and preview before any publish. No Gumroad connector/account status assumed.
learnings.next_measurement: Record the first real application of this gate (inputs, source URL fetched, result) and upgrade evidence_status only after that read-back.
learnings.title: HO-06 Gumroad draft-first ürün kapısı

learnings.claim: When a YouTube Analytics report uses the video dimension or a video filter, subscribersGained and subscribersLost include only subscribe and unsubscribe actions from that video watch page, not channel page or home guide actions.
learnings.decision: SUBSCRIBER_CONVERSION_GATE: after analytics maturity, record subscribersGained, subscribersLost, net subscribers, engagedViews, and net subscribers per 1000 engaged views when the denominator is positive. Label the result watch-page-attributed. Do not score a Short on raw views alone and do not treat a video-filtered net as total channel subscriber change or Shorts-feed attribution.
failure_history: Commit b1a9ff76 added subscriber conversion code and tests but left learning_ledger.json without a SUBSCRIBER_CONVERSION_GATE row.
fallback_history: If an authorized video-filtered Analytics query is unavailable, keep subscriber conversion unknown and do not infer it from raw views or channel-level subscriber change.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next authorized video-filtered Analytics read-back, store subscribersGained, subscribersLost, engagedViews, and the watch-page label. Do not invent numbers if the query fails.
learnings.title: Video-filtered subscriber metrics are watch-page only

learnings.claim: YouTube highlights intro, top-moment, spike and dip labels only when they are detected, and the video should be at least 60 seconds long and have at least 100 views. Audience retention data typically takes 1-2 days. A 25-30 second Short should not be expected to receive those highlighted labels even when video-level retention exists.
learnings.decision: KEY_MOMENTS_DURATION_GATE: for 25-30 second Shorts, do not wait for or require highlighted intro/top-moment/spike/dip labels. After processing, use available video-level retention plus stayed/chose-to-view, engaged views, AVD, APV and watch time. Classify missing highlighted labels on a sub-60-second Short as not_applicable_by_duration, not as an analytics failure.
failure_history: Markdown youtube-short-retention-key-moments-limit-2026-10-02 was on main without a learning_ledger row.
fallback_history: If highlighted key moments are absent on a sub-60-second Short, classify as not_applicable_by_duration and use the available retention curve or metrics. If retention itself is missing before 1-2 days, mark immature rather than zero.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next owned Short after at least 1-2 days, record retention_available, processing age, stayed-to-watch, engaged views, AVD, APV and watch time. Do not score missing key-moment labels as a failure when duration is under 60 seconds.
learnings.title: Shorts under 60 seconds do not get highlighted retention key moments

learnings.claim: The SEC EDGAR API page (fetched 2026-10-09) states data.sec.gov submissions and XBRL APIs need no authentication or API key and update in real time (submissions typically under one second, XBRL under one minute), and the SEC developer resources page limits each user to no more than 10 requests per second across all machines and blocks unclassified bots.
learnings.decision: FINANCE_EDGAR_PRIMARY_GATE: company earnings/filing claims in the Finans mail should be verified against data.sec.gov submissions/companyfacts before secondary news; the fetcher must stay well under 10 req/s and identify itself, and an IP block is reported as BLOCKED, not as no news.
fallback_history: If data.sec.gov blocks the runner, fall back to the EDGAR Latest Filings RSS and mark the item unverified.
learnings.next_measurement: Verify one 8-K headline from the next Finans mail against data.sec.gov and record latency between filing time and the news item.
learnings.title: SEC EDGAR keyless API with 10 req/s fair access

learnings.claim: URLs in Shorts descriptions and comments are non-clickable; a Related video link can be clickable in the Shorts player when advanced-feature access and eligibility are verified.
learnings.decision: Do not design a conversion CTA that depends on a raw description or comment URL; prefer native Related video only after access read-back.
fallback_history: Use a separately verified clickable surface; do not infer clickability from plain text.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next suitable Short, verify advanced-feature access before using Related video and do not claim conversion lift without owned analytics.
learnings.title: Shorts description and comment URLs are not the clickable route

learnings.claim: The official GraphQL Admin API reference (fetched 2026-10-09) states that the GraphQL API can return 200 OK for cases that would be 4xx/5xx in REST, with errors[].extensions.code values such as THROTTLED, ACCESS_DENIED, SHOP_INACTIVE and INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, that a single query above the max cost (1000) fails with MAX_COST_EXCEEDED, and that responses carry extensions.cost.throttleStatus.
learnings.decision: SHOPIFY_200_ERROR_GATE: never treat HTTP 200 as success; a response with a non-empty errors array or mutation userErrors is a failure classified by extensions.code. THROTTLED -> backoff/retry; MAX_COST_EXCEEDED -> split query or use bulk operation; ACCESS_DENIED/SHOP_INACTIVE -> stop and escalate to Furkan.
fallback_history: If Admin API access is blocked, use Shopify admin CSV exports as a manual fallback and mark data user_reported.
learnings.next_measurement: Add a fixture test for each code once a real error sample is captured from the store.
learnings.title: Shopify GraphQL errors arrive with HTTP 200

learnings.claim: Per-workflow concurrency groups prevent duplicate runs of one workflow but do not serialize different workflows that push to the same branch.
learnings.decision: Use one repo-main-writers group with queue max for all workflows that commit to main, while retaining pull-rebase as a secondary conflict check.
failure_history: Ten write-capable workflows used separate concurrency groups, allowing cross-workflow pushes to overlap.
fallback_history: If a queued run reaches the 100-run limit or stalls, stop the unhealthy writer and preserve the existing pull-rebase conflict path.
learnings.next_measurement: Verify workflow validation, successful CI, and the next scheduled writer runs without push conflicts or canceled pending jobs.
learnings.title: Repository writers need one queued concurrency group

learnings.claim: Shopify Help defines a returning customer as someone who placed an order and whose order history already includes at least one order. The Returning customers report lists customers with two or more orders. The One-time customers report lists customers with exactly one order. Returning customer rate is returning customers divided by customers. Cohort period 0 counts a repeat order in the same period as the first order. Customer reports other than New vs returning can lag about 12 hours, and customer-report history can include orders outside the selected timeframe.
learnings.decision: REPEAT_PURCHASE_GATE: do not treat a first order, a session, traffic, or an RFM group as a repeat purchase. A repeat purchase requires order history of at least two orders, or a returning-customer row whose history already included an order. Keep REPEAT_VALUE_GATE for the rate formula and COHORT_RFM_GATE for cohort versus RFM. Do not copy the Help 20-40 percent range as this store. Leave the store rate unknown until an authorized admin report is read.
failure_history: Mail said the Shopify repeat purchase gate could not be verified. REPEAT_PURCHASE_GATE was absent from the ledger. REPEAT_VALUE_GATE was already persisted and is not this token.
fallback_history: If admin reports are unavailable, leave repeat purchase unknown. Do not substitute industry rate, traffic, or RFM group.
learnings.next_measurement: On an authorized New vs returning customers and Returning customers read, store first-time count, returning count, rate, and customers with 2+ orders. Leave unknown if admin is not opened.
learnings.title: Repeat purchase is a second order, not a first order or an RFM group

learnings.claim: YouTube Analytics supports insightPlaybackLocationType so views and estimated watch time can be grouped by the page or application where playback occurred. Playback location is not the same dimension as insightTrafficSourceType and does not by itself prove why a video performed.
learnings.decision: PLAYBACK_LOCATION_CONTEXT_GATE: when authorized mature Analytics is available, pair views and watch time with insightPlaybackLocationType, compare like-for-like contexts, and do not merge playback location with traffic source. If authorized data is missing, keep location unknown.
failure_history: Markdown learn_youtube_playback_location_context_20261003 was on main without a learning_ledger row.
fallback_history: If authorized playback-location data is unavailable, keep location unknown and use existing engagedViews, retention, and traffic-source evidence without guessing location.
learnings.next_measurement: After Analytics maturity on a real Short, retrieve insightPlaybackLocationType with views and estimatedMinutesWatched and record whether conclusions change when contexts are separated. Do not query before the 48-72 hour window.
learnings.title: Playback location is context, not traffic source or causality

learnings.claim: Shopify Product Insights Customers compares first-time purchasers with customers who already have at least one past purchase, inside the last-90-day product view. Shopify Analytics defines returning customer rate as returning customers divided by customers. A first order is not repeat value, and traffic or public views are not repeat value.
learnings.decision: REPEAT_VALUE_GATE: do not score a product as repeat-valuable from first purchases, sessions, traffic source, or public views. When authorized store data exists, use returning customers divided by customers for the same window, and keep Product Insights Customers as first-time versus past-purchase counts, not lifetime value. Keep PRODUCT_SALES_SOURCE_GATE in force so repeat counts still need net sales and net units. Do not copy the Help page 20-40 percent range as this store.
failure_history: Before this write, learning_ledger had PRODUCT_SALES_SOURCE_GATE but no REPEAT_VALUE_GATE row.
fallback_history: If admin reports are unavailable, leave repeat value unknown. Do not substitute virality or a category benchmark.
learnings.next_measurement: On an authorized Product Insights and New vs returning customers read for the same window, store first-time count, returning count, returning customer rate, net sales, and net units. Leave unknown if admin is not opened.
learnings.title: Repeat value is returning customers over customers, not first purchase or traffic

learnings.claim: TRAFFIC_SOURCE_DETAIL_GATE: insightTrafficSourceType identifies how viewers reached a video; insightTrafficSourceDetail is populated only for supported source types and its meaning changes by source. SHORTS means referral by vertical swipe in the Shorts viewing experience, and the official detail list does not define insightTrafficSourceDetail for SHORTS. Do not infer a missing detail.
learnings.decision: TRAFFIC_SOURCE_DETAIL_GATE stays open. Interpret traffic source as a typed pair (source_type, source_detail). Never infer a missing detail. For Shorts-feed traffic, source_type=SHORTS is meaningful but detail stays unknown/not-applicable unless an official supported field or authenticated response proves otherwise. Markdown alone is not persistence. Human note learn_youtube_traffic_source_detail_gate_20261003 claimed write_read_back_pass before a ledger row existed; that claim was fail-closed.
failure_history: 2026-10-03 machine search: TRAFFIC_SOURCE_DETAIL_GATE was absent from learning_ledger.json while knowledge/learn_youtube_traffic_source_detail_gate_20261003.md already said persistence_status write_read_back_pass. learning_bridge.py gate exited fail closed.
fallback_history: If detail is unavailable, retain source_type plus mature aggregate engagedViews/watch-time/retention metrics; do not synthesize referrer/search/video detail.
learnings.next_measurement: On mature owned-channel data, query insightTrafficSourceType with engaged viewing/watch-time metrics; only for source types officially supporting detail, run source-specific detail queries and compare retention/AVD/APV without causal claims.
learnings.title: TRAFFIC_SOURCE_DETAIL_GATE

learnings.claim: Repository TinyFish analytics summary for Cerno 2026-09-11 through 2026-10-08 reports 5300 views, 9.5 watch hours, +6 subscribers; Mbappe Short 2610 views, airplane window 1219, airplane seat 1122. These are reported snapshots, not independently re-fetched Studio metrics in this run.
learnings.decision: Run three original 30-second moving-footage concept tests in order: (1) Mbappe sprint mechanics explained without copyrighted broadcast clips; (2) surprising airplane window phenomenon with verified factual explanation; (3) airplane seat hidden feature with original demonstration. Select the next video only after hook/storyboard and licensing QC. Compare engaged views, stayed-to-watch/swiped-away, average view duration, retention and subscribers; do not infer causality from view ranking alone.
failure_history: No direct YouTube Studio TinyFish browser analytics execution in this turn; 5300/2610/1219/1122 figures were read from Grok's committed 2026-10-09 report.
fallback_history: If fresh Studio metrics unavailable, label conclusions provisional and do not claim retention or swipe-rate improvements.
learnings.next_measurement: Retrieve fresh YouTube Studio per-video engaged views, stayed-to-watch, average percentage viewed, retention curve, and subscriber gains; compare these three concepts with the 2026-09-11 to 2026-10-08 baseline after publication.
learnings.title: Cerno Shorts: football and aviation topic tests from 28-day snapshot

learnings.claim: After the 2026-08-27 public view alignment, public views count from the first frame and must not be used as a substitute for engagedViews in quality or monetization comparisons.
learnings.decision: PUBLIC_VS_ENGAGED_VIEW_GATE: use public views for reach/start exposure and engagedViews plus AVD/APV/retention for quality; store metric name and definition date.
fallback_history: If engagedViews is unavailable, mark engaged performance unknown rather than substituting public views.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next authorized Short analytics read, fetch views and engagedViews for the same video and date window; do not infer engagedViews from public views.
learnings.title: Public views and engagedViews are not interchangeable after 2026-08-27

learnings.claim: SHORTS_RETENTION_FALLBACK_GATE is the lessons.md alias of KEY_MOMENTS_DURATION_GATE. Official YouTube Help says audience retention is video-level and typically takes 1-2 days; highlighted intro, top-moment, spike and dip labels are shown only when detected and the video should be at least 60 seconds with at least 100 views. AVD is calculated from engaged views and corresponding watch time. A sub-60-second Short must not treat missing automatic key-moment labels as a QA failure, and must not infer hook or payoff failure from public views.
learnings.decision: SHORTS_RETENTION_FALLBACK_GATE: keep learn_202ac32ebf4b8ee9 as the machine row. For sub-60-second Shorts, do not require automatic key-moment labels; after maturity use video-level retention curve or detailed activity plus stayed-to-watch, engagedViews, AVD, APV and watch time. Missing labels are not_applicable_by_duration. Do not infer hook or payoff failure from public views. Help-page 1-2 days does not replace the Analytics API 48-72 hour gate.
failure_history: Commit 3825f11 added lessons.md SHORTS_RETENTION_FALLBACK_GATE without a learning_ledger row, reusing a human learning_id.
fallback_history: If retention curve or detailed activity is unavailable or immature, mark it unknown and do not infer hook or payoff failure from public views.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next owned sub-60-second Short after analytics maturity, record retention curve or detailed-activity availability, stayed-to-watch, engagedViews, AVD, APV and watch time. Do not score missing key-moment labels.
learnings.title: Shorts retention fallback is the key-moments gate alias

learnings.claim: The YouTube Reporting API anonymizes some dimension values below privacy thresholds as NULL, ZZ, or US-ZZ, while preserving aggregate metrics in those rows; actual thresholds may change.
learnings.decision: REPORT_PRIVACY_SUPPRESSION_GATE: Treat NULL in privacy-suppressed traffic-source, age, gender or subscribed-status dimensions and ZZ/US-ZZ in geography dimensions as anonymized aggregate buckets, not malformed or missing rows. Preserve their numeric metrics in totals while keeping the underlying dimension unknown; never reconstruct hidden identities, locations, search terms or thresholds. Keep this rule distinct from header-only zero-data CSV handling. This is a documented ingestion rule, not proof of owned-channel Reporting API access or deployed parser behavior.
failure_history: 2026-10-08 earlier candidate promotion write was blocked before a commit; no persistent record was established.
fallback_history: Without authorized Reporting API CSV access, preserve this as an official documentation-based ingestion rule and do not invent channel-level data or a passing integration test.
learnings.next_measurement: On a permitted owned-channel Reporting API read, use header-mapped CSV parsing and compare aggregate totals with and without anonymized rows; verify no suppressed dimension is imputed. Until then production integration remains unverified.
learnings.title: Reporting privacy-suppressed dimensions preserve aggregate metrics

learnings.claim: YouTube Studio Advanced Mode exported reports contain at most 500 rows; a 500-row export must not be treated as complete when the underlying report could contain more rows, and YouTube Reporting API is the documented bulk alternative.
learnings.decision: YOUTUBE_STUDIO_EXPORT_500_ROW_GATE: A Studio Advanced Mode export containing 500 data rows reaches the documented limit; label completeness UNKNOWN/POSSIBLY_TRUNCATED rather than COMPLETE. Do not assume the unexported rows exist or calculate full-channel totals by summing that potentially capped file. If complete row-level bulk data is needed, use the YouTube Reporting API only after authorization and report compatibility are verified. Keep this separate from the Reporting API header-only no-data and privacy-suppression gates.
fallback_history: Without Reporting API authorization, report the 500-row cap and leave full dataset completeness unknown; do not invent missing rows or infer totals.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next authorized Studio export, count data rows, record report dimensions/time window, flag 500 as possibly truncated, and compare against a permitted Reporting API report or trustworthy channel totals when available. Until then real-channel completeness and ingestion are unverified.
learnings.title: Studio Advanced Mode export has a 500-row completeness limit

learnings.claim: YouTube Analytics API data is not real-time; processing typically adds 48-72 hours of latency, and responses omit recent days until all requested metrics are fully processed. Current per-video view, like, and comment counts belong to Data API videos.list, not Analytics.
learnings.decision: ANALYTICS_MATURITY_GATE: do not close retention or watch-time learning from Analytics API data before the documented processing window. Do not treat missing recent Analytics rows as zero. Use Data API or verified Studio state for current counts, then re-read Analytics after at least 72 hours.
failure_history: Markdown learning learn_youtube_analytics_latency_gate_20261002 was on main without a learning_ledger row, so the machine set could not discover it.
fallback_history: If authorized Analytics API is unavailable, use verified Studio analytics after sufficient processing time; otherwise mark the metric unknown and do not infer it from public views.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next authorized real Short, record publish time, a fast-state count where available, then Analytics after at least 72 hours. Only the mature read may close retention or watch-time learning.
learnings.title: Analytics API learning waits for the 48-72 hour processing window

learnings.claim: The Federal Reserve Board RSS page (fetched 2026-10-09) lists official feeds for all speeches and testimony, per-governor speeches, and data feeds for Foreign Exchange Rates (H.10) and Selected Interest Rates (H.15).
learnings.decision: FINANCE_FED_RSS_GATE: Fed rate/speech claims in the Finans mail are sourced from federalreserve.gov feeds first; secondary outlets (Investing.com etc.) are only context and must not be the sole source for a Fed statement.
fallback_history: If the feed is unreachable, use the federalreserve.gov newsevents page and mark freshness unknown.
learnings.next_measurement: Wire one Fed speeches feed into the finance runner and count items matched vs unmatched in the next three Finans mails.
learnings.title: Federal Reserve official RSS for speeches and rates

learnings.claim: Shopify Analytics session measurement rolled out 2026-09-21 to 2026-09-23. Sessions follow continued activity and end after 30 minutes of inactivity instead of always splitting at midnight UTC. Some sessions without a pageview are counted. Identified bot sessions are filtered from session reports by default. Conversion rate and other session-derived metrics can move even when orders, sales and customer counts do not. Historical data is not reprocessed; post-update session data is a new baseline. Bot classification applies only to sessions from 2025-10-07 onward.
learnings.decision: SESSION_MEASUREMENT_BASELINE_GUARD: timestamp the Shopify metric definition. Do not interpret a boundary jump in sessions, conversion rate, add-to-cart rate, reached-checkout rate, checkout conversion rate, bounce rate, pageviews per session, average session duration or online-store visitors across 2026-09-21..23 as demand change by itself. Cross-check orders, sales and customer counts. Compare post-update periods with the same human/bot filter where that filter exists. If metric version or filter state is unknown, mark the session-derived comparison non-comparable.
failure_history: Commit 158be857 added the guard only to knowledge/lessons.md. learning_ledger.json and source_catalog.json had no matching row on read-back.
fallback_history: If session metric version or human/bot filter state is unknown, do not compare session-derived rates and fall back to orders, sales and customer counts plus a post-update baseline.
learnings.next_measurement: After the store is public and an authorized Analytics read exists, compare only post-2026-09-23 like-for-like periods with the same human/bot filter, and record orders, sales and customers beside sessions. Do not invent store numbers.
learnings.title: Shopify session metrics need a post-2026-09-23 baseline

learnings.claim: YouTube Analytics subscribedStatus has SUBSCRIBED and UNSUBSCRIBED values that reflect subscription state at the time the user activity occurs. Channel reports can pair that dimension with engagedViews, views, estimatedMinutesWatched, averageViewDuration and averageViewPercentage only in documented combinations. The split is audience context, not proof that subscribing caused retention or watch time.
learnings.decision: SUBSCRIBED_STATUS_CONTEXT_GATE: after analytics maturity, compare like-for-like engaged viewing and watch-time quality for SUBSCRIBED versus UNSUBSCRIBED viewers only when an authorized report supports the combination. Keep the segment label and date window. Do not infer the split from public views or claim algorithmic causality.
failure_history: Markdown learn_youtube_subscribed_status_context_20261003 was on main without a learning_ledger row.
fallback_history: If authorized subscribed-status data is unavailable or the metric combination is unsupported, mark the split unknown and keep aggregate mature engagedViews, retention, AVD and APV.
learnings.next_measurement: After the Analytics maturity window on an owned Short, query a documented subscribedStatus combination and record engagedViews, watch time, AVD and APV where supported. If the combination is unsupported or unauthorized, mark the split unknown.
learnings.title: Subscribed status is audience context, not causality

learnings.claim: A digital product can be planned and quality-checked locally without Gumroad login, API token, payment setup, or publishing; live Gumroad product creation and sales metrics cannot be verified without account access.
learnings.decision:
Use these five secret-free preparation steps; no live Gumroad action is claimed:
1. Ürün adayı ve alıcı vaadini yaz: örnek Mutfağın Hammaddeleri; mevcut kitap bölümleri tamamlanmış gibi sunulmaz.
2. Orijinal içerik, telif, görsel lisansları ve dil tutarlılığı için kontrol listesi çıkar; eksik bölümleri taslak olarak işaretle.
3. İndirilebilir dosya taslağını (PDF/ePub uygunluğu), kapak brief'ini, örnek sayfayı ve açıklamayı yerel olarak hazırla; yükleme/yayın yok.
4. Fiyat, platform ücreti, net gelir ve iade koşullarını doğrulanmamış varsayımlarla ayrı tabloda planla; gerçek fiyat ve ödeme ayarını değiştirme.
5. Yayın öncesi QC: dosya açılıyor mu, bağlantılar çalışıyor mu, ürün açıklaması doğru mu, teslim dosyası tamam mı? Sonra gerçek Gumroad hesap erişimi/izin doğrulamasını bekle.
failure_history: No authenticated Gumroad connection, draft creation, sale, or payment configuration verified.
fallback_history: If API or account access unavailable, retain local product draft and mark publishing BLOCKED_USER or BLOCKED_EXTERNAL.
learnings.next_measurement: Verify current Gumroad product and upload API permissions against official docs; build local draft files, check content/licensing, then run account-connected draft-only smoke test if authorized.
learnings.title: HO-06 Gumroad draft-first digital product workflow without secrets or payments

learnings.claim: Without a Shopify store token, public official Shopify documentation can establish API field requirements, analytics definitions, rate limits, and safe read-only planning, but cannot reveal the user's live shop data or cohort metrics.
learnings.decision: Do the following five steps without secret or live store writes; only then request read-only store access if truly needed. Steps: (1) Create a read-only GraphQL field checklist for products, variants, inventory, orders, customers, and analytics; label required scopes and API version. [src_64dbdcaa3ac686c8] (2) Define cohort metrics (first vs returning customers, repeat purchase rate) and prevent unsupported claims about attribution. [src_0acc40a4a170ff80, src_d04b5a72ae4029f9] (3) Prepare a product-opportunity scoring template: demand, landed cost, shipping, return risk, gross/net margin, and evidence confidence; no live shop assumptions. [src_97a7eb010a0d1efa] (4) Write a public-docs-based GraphQL query skeleton with minimal fields and cursor pagination, but do not execute against store or request credentials. [src_64dbdcaa3ac686c8] (5) Specify rate-limit-aware retries and a dry-run validation fixture; 401/403 must block rather than retry repeatedly. [src_843ab9beadd1f15b]
failure_history: No live Shopify store query or customer/order data was accessed in this task.
fallback_history: If store read scope unavailable, retain templates and report BLOCKED_EXTERNAL instead of invented metrics.
learnings.next_measurement: Review the field checklist against current Admin GraphQL API version; verify real Shopify connection/scopes before any actual query; measure first read-only dry run and record evidence.
learnings.title: HO-05 Shopify: first five secret-free preparation steps

learnings.claim: POSIX flock protects processes sharing one checkout, while GitHub Contents API updates require the current blob SHA and serialized remote writes.
learnings.decision: Keep local flock plus atomic replace; remote writers must read the current blob SHA, write serially, and re-read after conflicts.
failure_history: A local file lock cannot coordinate independent GitHub runners or automation branches.
fallback_history: On conflict, fetch the new blob SHA and reassess the delta before one bounded retry.
learnings.next_measurement: Track HTTP 409 or 422 conflicts and verify successful read-back on the merged main branch.
learnings.title: Local and remote write locks are separate

learnings.claim: Rights clearance is necessary but not sufficient for revenue-targeted Shorts; substantive original contribution is also required, and optional music can change Creator Pool allocation.
learnings.decision: Before publish require commercial rights clearance and a distinct originality or reused-content gate; evaluate music only when it adds narrative or retention value.
fallback_history: If rights or originality cannot be verified, replace with original or licensed footage and original narration.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next Shorts production decision record rights source, originality evidence, and whether music is used.
learnings.title: Shorts revenue needs originality plus rights, and music is not revenue-neutral

learnings.claim: Authorized YouTube Analytics can segment owned-video discovery by insightTrafficSourceType and, for supported sources, insightTrafficSourceDetail. Raw views do not establish feed, browse, or search mix.
learnings.decision: Before changing packaging or distribution, classify discovery source only from an authorized report. Otherwise mark traffic source unknown. Do not invent search terms or external pages.

learnings.claim: YouTube Analytics sharingService is a core dimension that identifies the service used when a viewer shares a video through the YouTube or player Share button. The Reporting API channel_sharing_service_a2 report pairs sharing_service with the shares metric. Those events do not prove the recipient opened the link, watched, converted, or bought anything, and they are not unique people.
learnings.decision: SHARING_SERVICE_CONTEXT_GATE: when authorized mature Analytics or Reporting data exists, keep aggregate shares per engaged views and optionally break shares down by the documented sharingService or sharing_service dimension. Never infer clicks, recipients, sales, causality, or unique sharers from service-level share events. If the dimension is unavailable, keep aggregate shares and mark destination unknown.

learnings.next_measurement: On an owned mature Short, query a documented sharingService or channel_sharing_service_a2 shares combination. If unauthorized or unsupported, mark destination unknown.
learnings.title: Sharing service is Share-button destination context, not downstream proof

learnings.claim: YouTube Analytics youtubeProduct identifies the YouTube service where activity occurred. Documented values are CORE, GAMING, KIDS, MUSIC and UNKNOWN. Data starts 2015-07-18; UNKNOWN is activity before that date. YouTube Music before 2021-03-01 is CORE; Music on or after 2021-03-01 is MUSIC and real-time data is not recorded. Channel playback-details and some device-type reports may include youtubeProduct with creatorContentType and subscribedStatus. Playlist device-type reports do not list youtubeProduct. The dimension is not creatorContentType, traffic source, playback location, device type, a Shopify product, or a Shorts shopping sticker, and it does not prove causality, intent, or sales.
learnings.decision: YOUTUBE_PRODUCT_CONTEXT_GATE: when an authorized mature report supports the combination, keep youtubeProduct as a service segment beside creatorContentType. Do not assume every device report accepts it. If unauthorized or unsupported, mark product context unknown and do not infer it from public views.
failure_history: Markdown knowledge/learn_youtube_product_context_gate_20261003.md was on main without a learning_ledger.json row, so persistence_gate failed closed.
fallback_history: If authorized youtubeProduct data is unavailable, keep creatorContentType, engagedViews, retention and other verified context layers and mark product context unknown.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next owned-channel Analytics read after maturity, query a documented youtubeProduct combination with engagedViews and estimatedMinutesWatched. If the combination is unsupported or unauthorized, mark product context unknown.
learnings.title: YouTube product is service context, not content type or sales

learnings.claim: RELATIVE_RETENTION_BENCHMARK_GATE: when authorized mature retention data is available, inspect audienceWatchRatio across elapsedVideoTimeRatio buckets and relativeRetentionPerformance. Official metrics docs define audienceWatchRatio as watches of a portion divided by views; it can exceed 1 when a portion is rewatched, so it is not unique-viewer percent. relativeRetentionPerformance is 0-1 versus similar-length YouTube videos; 0 is worse than any, 1 is better than any, and 0.5 is the documented median. It is not an absolute retention percentage and does not prove recommendation lift, satisfaction, revenue, or sales. Do not infer these metrics from public views, AVD, or APV.
learnings.decision: CONSENSUS on the official definition. Markdown learning_id learn_youtube_relative_retention_benchmark_gate_20261003 on cb4173b is not the machine id. Metrics page checked 2026-10-03. Do not infer owned-channel relative retention.
fallback_history: If authorized bucketed or relative retention is unavailable, keep the comparative benchmark unknown and use verified aggregate AVD/APV/retention gates already in the pool.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next authorized mature owned-channel retention report, record elapsedVideoTimeRatio buckets, audienceWatchRatio, and relativeRetentionPerformance beside engagedViews, AVD/APV, shares/saves, and subscriber conversion. If the report is unavailable, leave the comparative benchmark unknown.
learnings.title: YouTube relative retention benchmark gate

learnings.claim: YouTube Audience analytics splits monthly unique viewers into new, casual, and regular. New viewers watched for the first time in the selected period, including private-browser, deleted-history, and over-one-year-absent viewers. Casual viewers watched at least once per month for 1 to 5 months in the past year. Regular viewers watched at least once per month for more than 6 months in the past year. Regular share can be below 1 percent for newer channels, trending videos, and Shorts-heavy channels. Audience segments do not affect reach or monetization. A low regular percentage is not failure, and audience mix is not proof that one Short caused loyalty.
learnings.decision: AUDIENCE_LOYALTY_GATE: add new/casual/regular mix and returning-viewer trend as a slower channel-level layer. Do not penalize a new or Shorts-heavy channel because regular viewers are initially very low. Do not promote a format to a durable series from audience mix alone. Promote only when mature per-video engagedViews, AVD/APV, retention, net subscriber conversion and deep engagement stay healthy and repeated publication coincides with improving returning/casual/regular evidence on like-for-like 7/28/90-day windows. Audience segments do not affect reach or monetization.

Markdown source_id youtube-help-audience-watch-behavior-2026 is not the machine source_id.
fallback_history: If authorized new/casual/regular or returning-viewer data is unavailable, keep loyalty state unknown and continue with verified per-video engagedViews, retention, subscriber conversion and deep-engagement gates. Never estimate audience segments from public views.
learnings.next_measurement: After an authorized Audience read exists, compare like-for-like 28-day windows after repeated original Shorts and record audience mix beside engagedViews, AVD/APV, retention, net subscriber conversion and deep engagement. Do not infer causality from mix alone.
learnings.title: YouTube audience loyalty is a channel-level new/casual/regular gate

learnings.claim: YouTube Analytics defines viewerPercentage as the percentage of viewers who were logged in when watching the video or playlist. It is a core metric. It is not averageViewPercentage, which is the average percentage of a video watched during a playback and excludes looping-clip traffic as of 2021-12-13.
learnings.decision: VIEWER_PERCENTAGE_SEMANTICS_GATE: keep viewerPercentage and averageViewPercentage as separate typed metrics. viewerPercentage is logged-in viewer share, not retention, completion, satisfaction, or subscriber share. If the field is unavailable, mark logged-in viewer share unknown. Do not substitute averageViewPercentage.
failure_history: Markdown learn_youtube_viewer_percentage_semantics_20261003 was on main with persistence_status standalone_write_read_back_pass_machine_ledger_unverified and no learning_ledger row. Cited source_id src_youtube_analytics_metrics_viewer_percentage is not the machine source id.
fallback_history: If authorized viewerPercentage is unavailable, leave logged-in viewer share unknown and continue with mature engagedViews, AVD, averageViewPercentage and retention without substitution.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next authorized mature owned-video Analytics read, request viewerPercentage only in a documented supported report and keep it separate from engagedViews, averageViewDuration, averageViewPercentage and retention. Do not infer a missing value.

learnings.claim: The official YouTube Reporting API bulk-reports page states that YouTube generates downloadable reports for days with no data, and those reports contain a header row but no additional data. The same page says column order must be read from the header row and new metric columns may appear.
learnings.decision: YOUTUBE_REPORTING_HEADER_ONLY_NO_DATA_GATE: classify a daily report with a valid header row and zero data rows as VALID_NO_DATA, not an API failure; do not retry it. A zero-byte or missing/malformed-header file is INVALID_EMPTY_FILE or INVALID_HEADER and must not be counted as zero activity. Map columns by header name, accept new metric columns, reject rows whose width differs from the header (INVALID_ROW_WIDTH). Preserve report id, createTime, startTime/endTime and provenance; on the same period prefer the newer createTime (backfill). Staged candidate learning_id learn_6ccf326aefe8c89e from Bilgi Kutuphanesi branch knowledge/library-20261008-csv-header-gate commit 1efab4b.
failure_history: ChatGPT Bilgi Kutuphanesi could not write the machine ledger (write block); candidate was staged only on a branch with persistence NOT PASS. Nobet denetcisi re-verified the official source on 2026-10-08 07:50 TRT and prepared this row via learning_bridge.py.
fallback_history: Without Reporting API access, do not infer zero activity from a missing file; mark the day unknown.
learnings.next_measurement: When an owned-channel Reporting API job exists, record per report: report id, createTime, header column count, data row count and classification. Until then keep ingestion integration unverified.
learnings.title: YouTube Reporting CSV header-only no-data gate

Playlist metrics are absolute event counts, include Watch Later, exclude automatic uploads/history lists, and are not unique viewers, purchases, or recommendation causality.

learnings.claim: YouTube Analytics defines cardClickRate as cardClicks divided by cardImpressions and cardTeaserClickRate as card teaser clicks divided by card teaser impressions. A card impression is logged when the card panel is opened, once per card. These rates do not use views or engagedViews as the denominator.
learnings.decision: CARD_METRIC_DENOMINATOR_GATE: preserve each documented denominator. cardClickRate = cardClicks/cardImpressions; cardTeaserClickRate = cardTeaserClicks/cardTeaserImpressions. Never substitute views, engagedViews, unique viewers, or each other. Do not infer viewer-level conversion. Human markdown id learn_youtube_card_metric_denominator_gate_20261003 is not the machine id. Owned-channel card metrics were not read.
failure_history: Markdown knowledge/learnings/youtube-card-metric-denominator-gate-2026-10-03.md at d78f057 had persistence_status machine_ledger_unverified and no learning_ledger row.
fallback_history: If authorized card metrics are unavailable or unsupported, mark card interaction context unknown and use mature engagedViews/watch-time/retention metrics without inventing a card CTR.
learnings.next_measurement: On a mature authorized owned-video Analytics read where card metrics are supported, retrieve cardClicks+cardImpressions and cardTeaserClicks+cardTeaserImpressions, recompute each documented rate, and compare only like-for-like surfaces. If unsupported or absent, mark unknown rather than zero.
learnings.title: Card rates use card impressions, not views

learnings.claim: UNIQUE_VIEWER_REACH_GATE: when authorized mature Studio Audience data exists, keep unique viewers as a separate estimated reach layer for like-for-like audience-size comparisons. Official Help defines unique viewers as the estimated number of viewers in the selected date range, calculated from engaged views and corresponding watch time. For Shorts, engaged views estimate people who stayed to watch. Unique viewers are not public views, engagedViews, subscribers, returning viewers, or unique reach/co-viewed views. Totals are available for periods up to 90 days and from 2017-08-01. Channel unique viewers dedupe a person who watched more than one video. Never invent unique viewers by dividing public views. Missing authorized values stay unknown.
learnings.decision: CONSENSUS on the metric definition. Markdown on 2c247ad9 was not a machine row. Official pages 9314416 and 7577916 checked 2026-10-03. Do not infer owned-channel unique viewers.
fallback_history: If authorized Studio Audience unique-viewer data is unavailable, keep unique viewers unknown and continue with verified engagedViews, retention and audience-loyalty signals.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next authorized mature owned-channel read, record the date window, unique viewers, engagedViews and watch time from the same comparable period. Do not use a window longer than 90 days. Keep the estimate label. If Studio Audience data is missing, leave unique viewers unknown.
learnings.title: YouTube unique viewer reach gate

learnings.claim: Shopify Customer cohort analysis groups customers by first-order date by default. Period 0 counts returning orders in the same period as the first order. RFM is a separate store-relative 1-5 score on recency, order count, and amount spent, mapped to 11 groups by R and floor of (F+M)/2. A cohort row is not an RFM group, and Prospects have no orders.
learnings.decision: COHORT_RFM_GATE: do not treat a first-order cohort, Product Insights Customers, or returning customer rate as an RFM group. Use Customer cohort analysis for acquisition-time retention, and RFM groups only from the store RFM report or rfm_group. Scores are quintiles of this store, not industry cutoffs. Keep REPEAT_VALUE_GATE and PRODUCT_SALES_SOURCE_GATE in force. Do not invent cohort or RFM numbers.
failure_history: Before this write, REPEAT_VALUE_GATE was persisted and COHORT_RFM_GATE failed closed.
fallback_history: Public Help and Admin GraphQL enum only. Store admin was not opened.
learnings.next_measurement: Read back python3 scripts/learning_bridge.py gate COHORT_RFM_GATE after the commit. An authorized store report is required before naming any cohort or RFM group for this store.
learnings.title: COHORT_RFM_GATE cohort month is not an RFM group

learnings.claim: Shopify Product Insights covers the last 90 days and shows net sales, net sales by channel, net units sold by traffic source, and first-time versus returning customers. Net units by traffic source can be negative when returns exceed sold units. The fetched Help page does not document Shopify app unavailability.
learnings.decision: PRODUCT_SALES_SOURCE_GATE: do not treat traffic volume or virality as product demand. When authorized Product Insights exists, cross-check traffic source against net units sold, net sales, sales channel, and new-versus-returning mix. Negative net units is a return-risk signal. Keep PUBLIC_VS_ENGAGED_VIEW_GATE, ANALYTICS_MATURITY_GATE, SHORTS_RETENTION_FALLBACK_GATE, and SESSION_MEASUREMENT_BASELINE_GUARD unchanged. If Product Insights is unavailable, do not substitute virality; use verified orders, sales, returns, landed cost, margin, trust, policy, and seasonality.
failure_history: Commit b3ac23eb added knowledge/video-shopify JSON only. learning_ledger.json and source_catalog.json had no PRODUCT_SALES_SOURCE_GATE row on read-back.
fallback_history: If authorized Product Insights is unavailable, keep source-level net-sales contribution unknown and fall back to verified orders, sales, returns, landed cost, shipping, margin, trust, policy, and seasonality. Never substitute virality.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next authorized product read-back, record 90-day net sales, net units by traffic source, net sales by channel, and new/returning mix. Do not invent store numbers if admin read is unavailable.
learnings.title: Product traffic is not demand until net units and net sales

learnings.claim: YouTube Reporting API device_type values are 100 unknown, 101 computer, 102 TV, 103 game console, 104 mobile phone and 105 tablet, with operating_system as a separate dimension. channel_device_os_a3 segments by device_type and operating_system. channel_combined_a3 documents playback_location_type, traffic_source_type, device_type and operating_system together as a Reporting API bulk schema. That documented bulk schema is not a license to invent an Analytics API query combination, and no authorized channel device query was run, so device mix remains unknown and is not algorithmic causality.

Use channel_combined_a3 only as a Reporting API bulk job, not as an assumed Analytics API cross-join. If device data is unavailable, mark device context unknown and do not infer it from public views.

learnings.claim: The official Gumroad API docs (fetched 2026-10-09) state that POST /v2/products publishes the product immediately unless draft=true or published=false, that PUT /v2/products/:id with files, tags or rich_content replaces the whole collection (omitted files are deleted), and that /v2/files/complete must not be retried because an upload_id works only once.
learnings.decision: GUMROAD_DRAFT_FIRST_GATE: any automated product create must send draft=true and wait for Furkan's approval before PUT /enable; product updates must resend every existing file id+url or omit files entirely; on a lost /files/complete response restart from /files/presign, never retry complete.
fallback_history: Without an OAuth token use the unauthenticated public /l/:permalink.json endpoint for read-only price/rating monitoring.
learnings.next_measurement: When a Gumroad token exists, create one draft product and read it back to confirm published=false before any further automation.
learnings.title: Gumroad create publishes immediately and PUT files replaces all

learnings.claim: The official YouTube Data API quota calculator (fetched 2026-10-09) states that search.list and videos.insert have their own quota buckets with a default of 100 calls per day at cost 1 per call, other endpoints share 10,000 units per day, invalid requests still cost at least one point, and daily quotas reset at midnight Pacific Time.
learnings.decision: SHORTS_UPLOAD_QUOTA_GATE: budget uploads against the separate 100/day videos.insert bucket, not the 10,000-unit pool; count failed/invalid calls too; schedule the quota-day boundary at 00:00 PT (10:00 TRT during PDT). Thumbnails.set (50) and videos.update (50) still draw from the shared pool.
fallback_history: If the upload bucket is exhausted, keep the rendered MP4 artifact and retry after the PT reset; never fall back to a paid tool.
learnings.next_measurement: On the first real upload run record quotaExceeded/uploadLimitExceeded errors and the Cloud console quota page value; until then upload quota is unverified for this project.
learnings.title: YouTube videos.insert own quota bucket

learnings.claim: Ten candidate public URLs are documented with keyless availability caveats. Public URL does not imply complete 2020-2025 coverage. CoinGecko global current data cannot prove historical dominance or TOTAL3; Binance OI history is restricted to recent history; exact historical DXY and daily Altseason Index archives remain unverified.
learnings.decision: No invented 0-100 values. For each indicator: reconstruct UTC daily x, freeze train-only lo=p20 and hi=p80 of preceding 730 daily observations (>=500 valid; at least 80% daily coverage), update only at quarterly walk-forward boundaries; monotonic up score=100*clip((x-lo)/(hi-lo)); down=100*clip((hi-x)/(hi-lo)). Index and breadth have natural 0/100 limits. If p20>=p80, unavailable history, or data lookahead risk, output N/A. Funding/OI requires historical OI and validated two-tail shape; N/A meanwhile. Hold out rolling next 90 days, every 90 days, from 2020-2025; do not calculate early folds lacking 730 days. Compare p10/p90 vs p20/p80 on train only, freeze choice before test. Prevent survivorship, data leakage, mixed providers, and unstable symbols.
failure_history: No 2020-2025 full raw history downloaded or backtest run in this task.
No verified keyless 2020-2025 series for exact DXY, daily Altseason Index, full-market BTC dominance/TOTAL3, and historical OI.

Grok 2026-10-10 URL check: stooq dx.f returned HTML not CSV; FRED fredgraph.csv timed out from Grok box; Binance fapi fundingRate/openInterestHist HTTP 451 (restricted location) from Grok box. Indicator list/directions moved to config/altcoin_panel_calibration.json.
fallback_history: If full historical series cannot be obtained, retain N/A rather than interpolate or fabricate a score.
learnings.next_measurement: Fetch URLs without secrets, archive source responses and daily coverage by year, establish valid as_of, then run 730d/90d walk-forward with baseline and report false alarms, precision/recall, and coverage. Any unverified endpoint/period remains blocked.
learnings.title: Altseason 10 indicators: free keyless source audit and 2020-2025 calibration protocol

learnings.claim: The official Gumroad API docs (fetched 2026-10-09) describe GET https://[seller].gumroad.com/l/:permalink.json as a public endpoint needing no authentication that returns display data (price_cents, ratings, is_published, options) and never seller-private or analytics fields; sales_count is null unless the creator shows it.
learnings.decision: GUMROAD_PUBLIC_MONITOR_PATH: read-only monitoring of a published product can start now via the public .json endpoint without secrets; do not infer sales from it (sales_count null means hidden, not zero).

learnings.claim: Shopify Admin GraphQL API 2026-10 adds return policy profiles: a set of return rules associated with markets that supersedes store return-policy text. Market.returnPolicyProfile returns only a directly assigned profile and is null when none is assigned; it does not resolve market hierarchy. Nullable returnRules or editRules mean those rules are turned off; null returnRules means customers can return without restriction. Reading requires read_legal_policies. Assigning a profile is a market edit and needs write_markets. There are no profile mutations; create, update, and delete stay in Shopify admin. A default profile covers markets without a named profile. Managed Markets EU profile is locked.
learnings.decision: MARKET_RETURN_POLICY_GATE: use authorized market-specific structured return rules as policy and trust context only. Never substitute policy terms, a return window, or a null profile for observed returned_quantity, return reasons, sales reversals, margin, or demand. A null Market.returnPolicyProfile is not proof that no return rule applies. Keep PRODUCT_SALES_SOURCE_GATE, REPEAT_PURCHASE_GATE, physical return versus sales-reversal separation, and Shorts analytics rules unchanged. Human learning_id learn_shopify_market_return_policy_gate_20261006.
fallback_history: If authorized market or profile data is unavailable, mark MARKET_RETURN_POLICY_UNVERIFIED and do not invent a return window.
learnings.next_measurement: On an authorized target-market read, capture the applicable return window and rules beside physical return metrics. Do not claim causality. If hierarchy or profile data is unavailable, mark MARKET_RETURN_POLICY_UNVERIFIED and do not invent a window.
learnings.title: Market return policy profiles are terms, not observed returns

learnings.claim: The official YouTube Analytics reports.query page banner says requests now require youtube.readonly, while the same page authorization-scope table and embedded JavaScript and Python samples still document yt-analytics.readonly. Documentation on that page is internally inconsistent, so the banner alone does not prove both scopes are always required.
learnings.decision: YOUTUBE_ANALYTICS_SCOPE_DOC_CONSISTENCY_GATE: narrow YOUTUBE_ANALYTICS_DUAL_SCOPE_GATE. Do not reauthorize solely because the reports.query banner exists. Keep runtime authorization unverified until an owned-channel reports.query response is observed. Classify a real 401/403 from returned error details and separate it from invalid_grant. Do not blind-retry. Human learning_id learn_youtube_scope_doc_consistency_20261003.
failure_history: Markdown knowledge/youtube-analytics-scope-doc-consistency-gate-2026-10-03.md cited unstable source_id src_google_youtube_analytics_reports_query_20261003 and had no learning_ledger row.
fallback_history: If authorized Analytics is unavailable, keep private Analytics fields unknown. Do not infer them from public metrics. Do not request new consent until a concrete API error shows a missing permission.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next authorized owned-channel reports.query, record status and error class only. If 401/403, classify missing-scope versus token failure from the response before any reauthorization.
learnings.title: reports.query scope docs are inconsistent; do not reauthorize from the banner alone
